question: Will the operating rooms of Hospital Privado de Mendoza be open for new surgeries on November 13, 2026?

calls.reasoning: As of 3 Nov 2026 the ministry-ordered suspension is still in force; no reopening date or timetable has been announced. The order runs until the investigation concludes, the epidemiology director said improvements must come first, no common source has been found, samples are pending at Malbran, cases rose to 5 confirmed with 2 deaths plus 2 under investigation, and families have gone to court, all pointing to a slow, cautious reopening. Against that, this is the main PAMI provider in the province, a partial reopening of one operating room counts, and outbreak-related closures often last only weeks; the suspension would be 22 days old by Nov 13. No market found.
calls.dossier:
- 21 Oct 2026: Mendoza health ministry activated an alert over post-surgical Serratia marcescens meningitis in patients operated at Hospital Privado (main PAMI provider in the province) and later treated at Hospital Central (Infobae 24 Oct).
- 22 Oct: inspection and samples taken; preventive suspension of all surgical activity 'until the technical and epidemiological investigation concludes'; the operating room and pharmacy were closed and materials seized (Infobae 24 Oct; La Nacion 26 Oct).
- 26 Oct: epidemiology director Falaschi said the operating room stays closed and will be used to improve surgical-area processes; leading hypothesis is a contaminated shared item (anesthetic, infusion, supplies) (La Nacion 26/28 Oct).
- 27 Oct: Los Andes reported 5 confirmed infections, 10 patients under watch, 4 deaths under study; surgery still suspended, no timeline.
- 28 Oct: La Nacion reported 'growing uncertainty about the origin'; no common source established; samples sent to Buenos Aires (Malbran).
- 29 Oct: Infobae reported two more deaths under investigation; operating rooms remain closed.
- 30 Oct: families filed a request for a judicial investigation (La Nacion).
- 3 Nov: Los Andes profiled a 59-year-old patient (hip surgery 14 Oct) who is critical; surgery still suspended; Malbran typing pending; focus on sterilization; no reopening info.
- Status quo as of 3 Nov: full suspension, no reopening date announced.
- For YES: PAMI dependence and pensioners' backlog create pressure; a partial or phased reopening of one operating room counts; remediation-based reopenings can happen before the investigation fully closes.
- For NO: source not identified, lab results pending, judicial and media scrutiny, case count still being revised.
- Base rate: no published dataset found for the reopening time of OR closures after outbreaks; anecdotal range is weeks to months.
- Resolves off ministry statements, hospital statements, or credible reports (ministry governs if reports conflict); evidence of scheduled surgeries actually performed counts. An unreported quiet reopening resolves NO.
- Event window: suspension from 22 Oct -> end of 13 Nov 2026 (UTC-3); as of 3 Nov, about 12 of 22 days (~55%) have elapsed.
- Searched but not found: any reopening announcement, any remediation completion report, any prediction market.
calls.reference_class: Regulator-ordered preventive operating-room closures after fatal hospital-acquired infection outbreaks (with source not yet identified), share reopened within ~3 weeks of closure

calls.reasoning: Status quo: suspension in force since Oct 22, open-ended 'until the investigation concludes'; as of ~Oct 30 no source identified, Malbrán genomic typing pending, epidemiology director says ORs need improvements before reopening, 5 confirmed cases, 2 extra deaths under study, criminal complaint filed. Reference class of nosocomial-outbreak OR closures: commonly 2-6+ weeks; source-unknown, fatal, judicialized cases skew longer. Counter: hospital is PAMI's main Mendoza provider, so pressure for a phased reopening is strong, and a partial reopening counts. No November reopening news found. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers: none).

calls.reasoning: Suspension ordered 22 Oct runs 'until the investigation concludes'. A 3 Nov Los Andes report (Run 1) confirms it is still fully in force with no timetable, the latest status any run found. No contamination source has been identified, Malbrán typing is pending, officials demand an overhaul of the surgical process first, the death toll may reach four, and a judicial complaint is open. All of that makes a ministry-approved reopening within 10 days unlikely. Upward pressure: this is PAMI's main surgical provider, and a phased reopening of one operating room counts. A reopening that is never reported resolves NO.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts. The only factual gap is how recent each run's status check was: Run 1 found a 3 Nov Los Andes report that surgery is still suspended with no reopening news, while Runs 2 and 3 only had reports up to about 30 Oct. I accept the 3 Nov report as the latest status, which leaves 10 days to the deadline. Whether the reference-class closure length of 2-6+ weeks reaches past 22 days is a judgment call. Unknown source, pending Malbrán results and the judicial case all push toward the long end, and an unreported reopening counts as NO. I land near Run 1's number, slightly above it for the chance of a phased single-room reopening driven by PAMI pressure.
